new_parts: GRIME (grime.py, 161 nodes): a new paint layer with the shared layer sockets, stacked last. It paints soot clouds over bricks AND mortar (each cloud has a solid middle that breaks into flat specks at its rim, two tones) and mottled mortar patches (gaps only). It is needed because MOSS and DAMAGE stop at the brick edge and COLOUR AND FADE lies under the mortar paint. It is about 3 times the inventory's 40-60 node estimate. The inventory's part 3 (low-spot darkening, for gravel) was not written.

BRICK HEIGHT RULE (height_rule.py, 13 nodes), a box after COMBINE: height = 2.533 x (grey - 38.7)/255. This is a straight line fitted once to the brick reference's stored 12-point height curve. It is needed because COMBINE's fixed slate rule cuts off 6.9% of dots at the top of the height range. In the same bakes it lifts the height group from 0.299 to 0.597 and overall from 0.538 to 0.654.

BRICK LAYOUT (brick_layout.py, 118 nodes): the small layout the task asked for. Half-brick running bond, each head joint moved by its own random amount (varied brick lengths), measured joint widths, rounded and dented edges; it hands over the eleven bundle numbers. It is optional: the shared slate LAYOUT by settings scores almost the same.

brick_recipe.py: copy of the slate recipe's wiring (shift, debug_view, tiles_across, stack_order kept) plus recipe.layout and recipe.height_rule. It refuses to run if any shared module was not imported from the snapshot.

judgement:
Brick needed no change to any shared layer. COLOUR AND FADE, DAMAGE, OUTLINE AND SHADOW and COMBINE ran unchanged from the snapshot (checksums OK, no cache folder written), with only their settings changed. MOSS ran unchanged but had no useful brick meaning, so it is off.

Three small new parts were needed:
- GRIME (161 nodes), for soot and mortar mottle that cross the gaps.
- A 13-node height box, because COMBINE's height-from-colour rule is fixed to slate. That is the one shared limit this trial found that no setting can fix.
- A 118-node brick layout, which was asked for but is optional: the shared slate LAYOUT by settings does almost as well.

84% of nodes are shared.

At a glance the tile reads clearly as an old red brick wall: running bond, mottled mortar, dark outlines, spalls and soot. The 2x2 repeat shows no seams.

It still trails the brick's own earlier recipe: 0.654 overall (0.615 mean over three seeds) against 0.725, and colour 0.642 (mean 0.584) against 0.750. The weak points:
- soot is small flecks, not smudges running down several courses;
- DAMAGE's slate lower-edge bias puts spalls as pale bands along the lower edges;
- patches inside the bricks have cut-paper edges;
- the right-hand shadow is missing;
- height follows colour too exactly because a shader cannot blur.

The seed alone moves the colour group from 0.516 to 0.642. It is a large step up from the first layered brick (0.194).

Tests:
- Half-tile shift test at 512: the tile repeats (colour 0.03% of dots differ by more than 40, against 31% for the control). GRIME mask differences are scattered speck-edge sampling, not a seam.
- Independence with Amount 0: no colour change outside each layer's own mask.
